small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_OW configs (e.g. 256) with BLOCK_OC=32/64 to amortize weight loads across more output spatial elements; current best tile likely under-utilizes the K=IC*KD*KH*KW dot.
- Try swapping the reduction order so IC is the inner GEMM-K (use tl.dot on [BLOCK_OC, IC] x [IC, BLOCK_OW]) without the tl.trans on x_vals — eliminates a transpose per (kd,kh,kw) iteration.
- Sweep num_stages=4 with num_warps=8 on the larger tiles; the inner static loop has 27 iterations and benefits from deeper pipelining on a bandwidth/L2-bound conv.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col-GEMM where K = IC*KD*KH*KW is reduced in a single tl.dot per BLOCK_K chunk, instead of 27 separate small dots over KD*KH*KW. This lets Triton issue one big mma per K tile and dramatically improves arithmetic intensity.
- Switch the program tiling to (N*OD, OC tile, OH*OW tile) and keep output channels-last so writes coalesce; precompute per-K-element input gather offsets once per program rather than recomputing inside three nested static_range loops.
- Consider a persistent kernel that loops over output spatial tiles per (N, OC) block to reuse the loaded weight tile across many spatial positions, since the weight tensor (64*32*27 ≈ 55K floats) easily fits in registers/SMEM and is reused OD*OH*OW times.
